text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.

- Eastern Slavonia Serbs will be exempt from serving in the Croatian army for the first two years following the enclave's reintegration with Croatia, the government said in its human and minority rights package sent to the U.N.
- Croatia has accepted American initiative for the cooperation of southeastern European countries, but will not agree to form any political associations or unions.

- National Judicial Council dismisses Krunoslav Olujic as the Supreme Court head after ruling he stained the court's reputation. Olujic allegedly "engaged in sex with minors and associated with people who have a criminal past".
- The government will support demands from industrial firms to give them preference in public projects, says Economy Minister Davor Stern.
- January to September 1996 total income of large firms and public sector enterprises estimated at 70.3 billion kuna, up 6.0 percent from the same period last year.
- There were 269,263 jobless in Croatia in December, or 8.1 percent more than in the same month of 1995. More than half of the unemployed were women.
- There were 14,282 abortions in 1995, compared to 26,223 in 1992. But Parliament is soon to discuss a new bill proposed by the Party of Rights on radically limiting abortions rights.
- Electrical concern Koncar to follow in the drugs firm Pliva's footsteps in its privatisation and listing abroad.
- Companies threaten to push one another into liquidation according to new legislation unless debtors pay up their liabilities. A shortage of bankruptcy experts expected.
- Stock exchange sees a new bull run. Hardly any liquid stocks are stagnating, let alone declining.
- Banking sector may become a new focus for investors in Croatia: Insurer Croatia Osiguranje announces the sale of a 50 percent stake in Hrvatska Gospodarska Banka.
- Parliament is soon to discuss a bill on euthanasia.
- Head of the Parliament's legal committee Vladimir Seks will propose a provision on castration of multiple rapists to be included in the penal code.
- Italian PM Romano Prodi and a delegation of Italian businessmen to visit Zagreb on Thursday.

- Instead of trying to lure British and American tourists, Croatia should concentrate on German and Central European markets, says Selimir Ognjenovic, director of I.D. Riva Tours in Munich. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
